attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

cases.label: date boundaries: start dates 0001-01-01, 1752-12-31, 1753-01-01, 2000-02-29 and 9999-12-31; end dates 0001-01-01, 1900-01-01 and 9999-12-31
cases.reasoning: date covers 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 on both engines (wider than datetime). Values before 1753 and the leap day check the date mapping and how both drivers read early years (a client that builds dates with Date.UTC maps years 0-99 to 1900-1999). only histories with EndDate NULL are listed.

cases.label: an end date equal to the start date, and one a day after it: the view does not compare the two
cases.reasoning: Neither view compares EndDate with StartDate; a conversion that added a validity check written as EndDate > StartDate, or that treated the end date as exclusive, would drop the history that starts and ends on 2010-06-15. Both rows respect the source check EndDate >= StartDate. Only histories with EndDate NULL are listed. 9999-12-31 is the end date of one row.

cases.label: NULL versus '': Title, MiddleName and Suffix as NULL and as ''; an empty department name and group
cases.reasoning: Each nullable text column is sent as NULL for one person and '' for another; Department.Name and GroupName are NOT NULL and sent as ''. '' must stay '' and NULL stay NULL on both engines.

null-vs-empty.detail: empty string: yes; NULL in a text input: yes

cases.label: text returned as stored: a department name and group names differing only in case, trailing spaces, non-ASCII and an emoji
cases.reasoning: No text is compared in the view. Department names are distinct (the source keeps Department.Name unique under its case-insensitive collation); the case-only pairs are department 'Sales' against groups 'SALES' and 'sales', and the first names 'Ann ', 'ANN' and 'ann'. A conversion that case-folded, trimmed or grouped text would differ. 'Marketing ' and 'Sales and Marketing ' end in a space; an emoji and an accent check the nvarchar -> varchar load on both engines.

cases.label: duplicate history rows (same employee, department and start date twice): two identical output rows
cases.reasoning: EmployeeDepartmentHistory has no key constraint in the scratch tables, so the same row twice is two rows on both engines; the view has no DISTINCT. Compared as a multiset.

top-ties.detail: two rows of HumanResources.EmployeeDepartmentHistory share BusinessEntityID = 1

cases.label: smallint and int extremes: departments -32768 and 32767, employees 0 and 2147483647
cases.reasoning: DepartmentID is smallint (smallint on PostgreSQL), BusinessEntityID int; the keys jump and sit at the type limits. A narrowing or sign error in the mapping would drop or change rows.

cases.label: rows dropped by the inner joins: a history for a missing department, a missing person; a person who is not an employee
cases.reasoning: Department, Person are inner joins. Department 9 does not exist, employee 4 has no Person row; those rows are dropped. Employee 5 has a Person row but no Employee row and is not listed.

objections.text: The label says the input includes EndDate 0001-01-01, but no EmployeeDepartmentHistory row sends that end date. The only 0001-01-01 value is a StartDate; the sent EndDate boundaries are 1900-01-01 and 9999-12-31.
objections.resolution: A01 now includes a history whose StartDate and EndDate are both 0001-01-01, so the label matches the sent end-date boundary and the row satisfies EndDate >= StartDate.

objections.text: The first history ends on 2010-06-14 after starting on 2010-06-15. It violates the source EmployeeDepartmentHistory check requiring EndDate >= StartDate (or NULL), so the case's central input cannot occur under the source schema preconditions.
objections.resolution: The first history now starts on 2010-06-14 and ends on 2010-06-15; all sent histories satisfy the source date check while retaining the equal-date boundary attack.

objections.text: Department names 'Sales', 'SALES' and 'sales ' collide under the source case-insensitive, trailing-space-insensitive unique key on HumanResources.Department.Name. The input cannot occur in the source table with its constraints.
objections.resolution: A04 now uses distinct department names. Its case-only pairs occur across Department.Name, GroupName, and Person.FirstName, so no source unique key is violated.
